title: Cystolitholapaxy (bladder stone)
subtitle: Break the stone, clear every fragment, and treat the cause

sources.title: EAU Guidelines on Management of Non-neurogenic Male LUTS
BAUS procedure-specific patient information and consent guidance

indications: A symptomatic or obstructing bladder stone.
contraindications: A stone too large for endoscopic clearance in reasonable time (open or percutaneous cystolithotomy).
preparation: Imaging for size and number, and ultrasound for upper tracts.
Consent: bleeding, infection, bladder injury, residual fragments, and treatment of the cause (often the prostate).
equipment: Cystoscope or nephroscope, holmium laser or pneumatic lithotripter, Ellik evacuator, three-way catheter.
anatomy: Bladder neck, prostate, trigone and ureteric orifices, bladder diverticula.
criticalSafety: Keep the energy on the stone and off the bladder wall.
Look for the cause: outflow obstruction, diverticulum, foreign body, or a tumour hidden under the stone.
commonErrors: Lasering with the bladder wall in front of the fibre.
postop: Outflow treatment if obstruction was the cause.

steps.emphasis: Note stone size and number, the prostate, any diverticulum, and the bladder mucosa.
In the bladder: fibre on the stone, the bladder moderately full, the wall never in front of the fibre.
Evacuate fragments with the Ellik and recheck every part of the bladder.
A catheter for drainage; a three-way catheter if bleeding.
Record clearance, the cause found and the plan to treat it.

step.clp.cause.title: Find and treat the cause
step.clp.cause.why: Bladder stones usually form behind outflow obstruction or in stagnant urine. Without treating the cause they come back, and a tumour may hide under the stone.
how: Once the stone is cleared, inspect the mucosa where it lay for tumour.
Assess the prostate and the bladder neck, look for diverticula, foreign bodies or a retained stent.
Treat obstruction now (for example TURP or HoLEP in the same sitting if consented) or book it.
pitfalls: Clearing the stone and missing a tumour under it.
